nodes.characterization_summary: All M/g-CN catalysts show negative formation energy Ef indicating thermodynamic stability with robust metal anchoring; clear charge transfer observed via Bader analysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1(c) displays the Ef for M/g-CN (the detailed Ef values for preferable anchoring sites are listed in Table S1 in the SI). As can be seen, all Ef values are negative, suggesting that the metal atoms can be steadily anchored in the cavity of g-CN with robust capability of suppressing the diffusion and aggregation. Additionally, Bader charge analysis indicates that there is clear charge transfer between the metal and g-CN

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine g-CN band gap 3.24 eV; M/g-CN (M=Ti, Ni, Ru, Pd, Os) band gaps reduced to 1.64-2.69 eV suitable for visible light absorption; CBM positions: Ti (-2.88 eV), Ni (-2.81 eV), Ru (-2.83 eV), Pd (-2.75 eV), Os (-2.93 eV), all > -4.44 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The band structures are calculated through HSE06 hybrid functional ... Compared with the band gap for pristine g-CN (3.24 eV), the band gaps for M/g-CN are significantly reduced. Especially for M/g-CN (M = Ti, Ni, Ru, Pd, Os), the systems exhibit semiconducting characteristics with band gaps in the range of 1.64-2.69 eV ... As shown in Fig. 2(m), the CBM for M/g-CN (M = Ti, Ni, Ru, Pd, Os) are located at -2.88, -2.81, -2.83, -2.75, and -2.93 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: Transition metal M/g-CN: valence bands from N p + M d orbitals, conduction bands from N p orbitals with strong N-M d orbital hybridization; main d orbital peaks near Fermi level enhance conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the transition metals, i.e., M (Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Y, Zr, Nb, Mo, Ru, Rh, Pd, Ag, Hf, Ta, W, Re, Os, Ir, Pt, Au), the valence bands are originated from N p and transition metals d orbitals, and the conduction bands stem from N p orbitals. There exists obvious hybridization between N p orbitals and transition metals d orbitals ... Above all, the main peaks for metal atoms d orbitals around the Fermi level can facilitate the electron transfer, further enhancing the electrical conductivity.

nodes.characterization_summary: HER Gibbs free energy ΔG_H* at pH=0: Ti/g-CN (-0.04 eV), Ni/g-CN (0.39 eV), Ru/g-CN (-0.48 eV), Pd/g-CN (0.07 eV), Os/g-CN (-0.57 eV); all values indicate thermodynamically favorable HER vs photogenerated electron driving force.
nodes.evidence_snippet: for M/g-CN (M = Ti, Ni, Ru, Pd, Os) systems, ΔG_H* are calculated to be -0.04, 0.39, -0.48, 0.07, and -0.57 eV, respectively at pH = 0. Since U_e for M/g-CN (M = Ti, Ni, Ru, Pd, Os) systems at pH = 0 is all larger than the corresponding ΔG_H*, the HER on these systems are thermodynamically spontaneous under natural sunlight irradiation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Water dissociation energy barriers Ea: Sc/g-CN (0.04 eV), Ti/g-CN (0.01 eV), V/g-CN (0.40 eV), Ga/g-CN (0.36 eV), Sn/g-CN (0.38 eV), Au/g-CN (0.43 eV), all < Pt(111) (0.95 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through CI-NEB calculations, the calculated Ea ... for M/g-CN (M = Sc, Ti, V, Co, Ga, Rh, Pd, Sn, Au) are 0.04, 0.01, 0.40, 1.53, 0.36, 2.04, 2.37, 0.38, and 0.43 eV, respectively. Compared with the commercial Pt (111) (0.95 eV), M/g-CN (M = Sc, Ti, V, Ga, Sn, Au) exhibit smaller Ea in alkaline conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Machine learning RFR model (R²=0.99) predicts ΔG_H* with feature importance: charge transfer Q (0.325) > electronegativity EN (0.155) > covalent radius (0.145) > d-band center (0.107).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As presented in Fig. 4(a), the R² and RMSE for training sets are 0.99 ... the importance of features are ranked in the order of Q (0.325) > EN (0.155) > r_cov (0.145) > εd (0.107) > Nva (0.094) > EI (0.090) > ICOHP (0.084).
